title: A population evolving
sub: Maximize height. Each dot is one individual: a 12-bit string decoded to a position.

frames.caption: Generation 0: 20 random 12-bit strings, each decoded to a position (4,096 possible strings in all). Nobody is near the tallest peak.

Generation 1. Each child: pick two parents by tournament (the fitter of two random individuals), cross over at a random cut, e.g. 010101|101001 + 110000|110010 → 010101110010, then mutate (flip each bit with probability 1/12) → 010101111010. The best individual is copied over unchanged (elitism).
Generation 2: fitter individuals win more tournaments and have more children, so the population drifts uphill.
Generation 3: a child lands on the tallest peak's slope (green). It is a recombined, mutated mix of two parents from lower ground.
Generation 10: the newcomer's descendants take over. Selection copies what works; the average climbs.
Generation 11: the newcomer's descendants take over. Selection copies what works; the average climbs.
Generation 12: the newcomer's descendants take over. Selection copies what works; the average climbs.
Generation 13: the newcomer's descendants take over. Selection copies what works; the average climbs.

Generation 14: 16 of 20 individuals are now on the tallest peak. Over 100 runs from random populations, this GA found the global peak 94% of the time, using 20 × 15 = 300 evaluations per run out of 4,096 possible strings.
